question.problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -3 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 8 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $u$ and $w$ are orthogonal. Find $(u+2w)\cdot (u-4v)-u\cdot u.$
question.worked_solution:
Since $u$ and $w$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that $u\cdot w=0.$ Therefore, using linearity of the dot product to expand the parentheses, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(u+2w)\cdot (u-4v)-u\cdot u & =u\cdot u+(2w)\cdot u-u\cdot (4v)-(2w)\cdot (4v)-u\cdot u \\  & =2(w\cdot u)-4(u\cdot v)-8(w\cdot v) \\  & =0-4(u\cdot v)-8(w\cdot v) \\  & =-4(u\cdot v)-8(w\cdot v) \\  & =-4((-5)\cdot 1+(-3)\cdot (-3)+2\cdot (-4)+0\cdot 1) \\  & -8(2\cdot 1+2\cdot (-3)+8\cdot (-4)+3\cdot 1) \\  & =-4(-5+9-8+0)-8(2-6-32+3) \\  & =16+264 \\  & =280.\end{aligned}
$$
